title: Scalar spectral measures of a separable positive generator under countable choice

references.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, section 2.3, Theorems 2.3.12 and 2.3.19, PDF pp. 31–34; standard spectral-interface context only. The separable Countable-Choice scalar construction is proved locally. Downloaded full PDF, read these pages for this interface.

statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal H\ne\{0\}$ be a separable complex Hilbert space with inner product linear in its first argument. Let $K:D(K)\to\mathcal H$ be densely defined, self-adjoint and positive, meaning $\langle Kx,x\rangle\ge0$ for $x\in D(K)$. Let $(U_t)_{t\in\mathbb R}$ be a strongly continuous unitary group with generator $iK$: its strong derivative at zero exists exactly on $D(K)$ and equals $iKx$. The spectrum $\sigma(K)$ is the complement of the set of $z$ for which $K-z:D(K)\to\mathcal H$ has a bounded everywhere-defined inverse.

For every $x,y\in\mathcal H$ there is a finite complex Borel measure $\mu_{x,y}$ on $[0,\infty)$ such that

$$\langle U_t x,y\rangle=\int_{[0,\infty)}e^{itE}\,d\mu_{x,y}(E),\qquad |\mu_{x,y}|([0,\infty))\le\|x\|\,\|y\|.$$

The measures are sesquilinear in $(x,y)$, $\mu_x:=\mu_{x,x}$ is positive with total mass $\|x\|^2$, and every $\mu_{x,y}$ is carried by $\sigma(K)$. If $P_0$ is the orthogonal projection onto $\ker K$, then

$$\mu_{x,y}(\{0\})=\langle P_0x,y\rangle.$$

In particular, if $\sigma(K)\subseteq\{0\}\cup[g,\infty)$ with $g>0$, the measures $\mu_{(I-P_0)x,(I-P_0)y}$ are carried by $[g,\infty)$. Spectral measures and a projection-valued spectral resolution are not assumptions of this statement.

title: Gaussian frequency separation of connected ground correlations

references.title: Bruno Nachtergaele and Robert Sims, Lieb–Robinson Bounds and the Exponential Clustering Theorem, arXiv:math-ph/0506030v3; section 3.2, PDF pp. 7–10, Gaussian separation and Lemma 1; the scalar regularization proof is reconstructed locally. Full 12-page article retrieved and read.

statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal A$ be a unital complex $C^*$-algebra with a strongly continuous automorphism group $\alpha_t$. Let $\pi:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ be a contractive unital $*$-representation on a separable Hilbert space, with linear-first inner product, and let $\Omega$ be a unit vector. Suppose a strongly continuous unitary group $U_t$ implements $\pi(\alpha_t(A))=U_t\pi(A)U_t^*$, fixes $\Omega$, and has positive self-adjoint generator $iK$ satisfying

$$\ker K=\mathbb C\Omega,\qquad \sigma(K)\subseteq\{0\}\cup[g,\infty),\qquad g>0.$$

Write $\omega(A)=\langle\pi(A)\Omega,\Omega\rangle$. Let $A,B\in\mathcal A$ commute, put $f(t)=\omega([A,\alpha_t(B)])$, and suppose $|f(t)|\le L|t|$ for $|t|\le\eta$, for some finite $L$ and $\eta>0$. For every $q>0$, the scalar integral

$$I_q(A,B):=\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{e^{-qt^2}}{2\pi it}\,f(t)\,dt$$

is absolutely convergent, with any value assigned to its integrand at $t=0$, and satisfies

$$\left|\omega(AB)-\omega(A)\omega(B)-I_q(A,B)\right|\le\|A\|\,\|B\|e^{-g^2/(4q)}.$$

The gap is that of this infinite- or finite-dimensional representation; no finite-volume approximating gaps are assumed.

title: Exponential connected clustering from a unique infinite-volume ground-state gap

references.title: Bruno Nachtergaele and Robert Sims, Lieb–Robinson Bounds and the Exponential Clustering Theorem, arXiv:math-ph/0506030v3; Theorem 2, PDF p. 4, complete section 3.2 proof pp. 7–10, and section 4 pp. 10–11; local weighted-norm constants and Countable-Choice construction are retained. Full 12-page article retrieved and read.

Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, section 4.4, Theorem 4.4.1, PDF pp. 105–106; statement and uniqueness qualification read, no clustering proof supplied there or imported here.

statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the finite-matrix $C^*$-identity used by the quasi-local completion. Let $\mathcal A$ be the quasi-local algebra of uniformly finite-dimensional spins on $\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge1$, with max-coordinate distance $d_\infty$. Let $\alpha_t$ be a strongly continuous automorphism group satisfying the exponential Lieb–Robinson estimate

$$\|[A,\alpha_t(B)]\|\le\frac{2\|A\|\|B\|}{C}(e^{v|t|}-1)\sum_{x\in X,\,y\in Y}F_a(d_\infty(x,y)),\qquad F_a(r)=e^{-ar}(1+r)^{-d-1},$$

for disjoint finite nonempty $X,Y$, $A\in\mathcal A_X$, $B\in\mathcal A_Y$, all real $t$, and fixed $a,C>0$, $v\ge0$. In particular this holds for the thermodynamic dynamics of a bounded finite-range interaction $\Phi$, with $C=C_{F_a}$ and $v=2C\|\Phi\|_{F_a}/\hbar$ from the weighted commutator theorem and any $\hbar>0$.

Here a **positive-energy ground state** means an algebraic state $\eta$ admitting a contractive unital $*$-representation $\pi$ on a complex Hilbert space, a unit vector $\Omega$, and a strongly continuous unitary group $U_t$ fixing $\Omega$, such that $\eta(A)=\langle\pi(A)\Omega,\Omega\rangle$, $\pi(\alpha_t(A))=U_t\pi(A)U_t^*$, and the generator is $iK$ for a positive self-adjoint densely defined $K$. Inner products are linear in their first argument. Such a representation can be restricted to the cyclic subspace generated by $\Omega$; no spectral resolution is included in the definition.

Suppose $\omega$ is the unique positive-energy ground state and its cyclic ground representation has an infinite-volume energy gap $\gamma>0$: writing $H=\hbar K$, require

$$\sigma(K)\subseteq\{0\}\cup[g,\infty),\qquad g=\gamma/\hbar>0.$$

Then for every pair of disjoint finite nonempty supports, with $r=\operatorname{dist}_\infty(X,Y)\ge1$, one has

$$|\omega(AB)-\omega(A)\omega(B)|\le\|A\|\|B\|\left(\frac{2|X||Y|}{\pi C}+1+\frac{2v+g}{\pi a g r}\right)e^{-\mu r},\qquad \mu=\frac{ag}{2v+g}>0.$$

This is exponential connected clustering for the infinite-volume state. The hypotheses do not require uniformly gapped finite-volume approximations, translation invariance, or a particular choice of finite-volume boundary ground states. The same estimate holds for any positive-energy state representation with $\ker K=\mathbb C\Omega$ and the stated gap, even without uniqueness among all ground states. Uniqueness is a sufficient hypothesis for that kernel condition, proved below. For other weighted interactions the assertion applies whenever their strongly continuous dynamics and the displayed Lieb–Robinson estimate are supplied; no missing thermodynamic-existence theorem for a general interaction is assumed to have been proved here.

For physical bookkeeping $t$ is in seconds, $H,\gamma$ are in joules, $\hbar$ is in joule-seconds and $K,g,v$ have inverse-second units. Lattice distances, $a,C,\mu$ and the exponential argument are dimensionless. The theorem does not prove a gap or uniqueness for an unspecified physical model.

title: A degenerate gapped Ising ground mixture does not cluster

references.title: Bruno Nachtergaele and Robert Sims, Lieb–Robinson Bounds and the Exponential Clustering Theorem, arXiv:math-ph/0506030v3; section 4, PDF pp. 10–11, degenerate-ground-space qualification as context only; the Ising example and its cyclic representation are constructed locally. Full 12-page article retrieved and read.

statement:
A nonzero excitation gap alone forces ordinary exponential connected clustering for every positive-energy ground state of a uniformly bounded finite-range spin-$\tfrac12$ chain on $\mathbb Z$, even when its ground space is degenerate. In particular there must be constants $C_0<\infty$ and $\mu>0$ such that

$$|\omega(Z_0Z_r)-\omega(Z_0)\omega(Z_r)|\le C_0e^{-\mu r}\qquad(r=1,2,\ldots),$$

where $Z_j=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$ is the Pauli observable on site $j$ and the ground representation has a positive self-adjoint generator with spectrum contained in $\{0\}\cup[g,\infty)$ for some $g>0$.
